full_judgment:
2. It is stated in the petition that the opposite parties filed a title suit being Title suit No. 73 of 1976 which was decreed on contest on 30.09.1980. In due course, the decree-holder-opposite-party filed an execution case being the Execution Case No. 18 of 1980. On appeal being the First Appeal no 20 of 1981, it was decreed in part on 07.07.1996. Thereafter, the judgment debtor petitioner filed an appeal before the Appellate Division being the Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No 689 of 1996 which was ultimately rejected on 16.03.1997 and a review petition being the Civil Review Petition no. 14 of 1997 was filed which was dismissed for default in pursuance to an order dated 16.11.2000. In the meantime, the decree holder opposite party filed another execution case on 08.06.2002 being the Title Execution Case no 3 of 2002 but on their prayer for withdrawal made on 08.08.2002 the said execution case was rejected on 03.09.2002 (Annexure-B). The decree-holder opposite parties also by their application dated 08.08.2002, prayed for vacating the earlier order of stay in Title Execution Case no 18 of 1980 passed on 19.12.1980 and by another application prayed for amendment of the petition of the execution case and also prayed for deputing a Magistrate with a police force along with an Advocate Commissioner. The learned Judge after hearing by his order dated 03.09.2002, allowed the amendment and re-started the Title Execution Case on 18 of 1980. On 15.09.2002 the judgment debtor petitioner filed an application praying for rejecting the Execution Case no 18 of 1980 as barred by limitation (Annexure-C). On hearing, the learned Joint District Judge, Comilla, by his order dated 28.09.2002 rejected the said petition as not maintainable and directed issuance of writ of delivery of possession in favour of the decree-holder-opposite-parties. 

 3. Mr. Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, Senior Advocate appears with Mr. Horandra Nath Nondy, Advocate, on behalf of the petitioners. He submits that according to the provisions of Article 182 of the Limitation Act, An execution case has to be filed within three years from the date of the decree or to take some steps in aid of the execution of the said decree within the next three year but the Execution Case No 18 of 1980 although was filed within the period of limitation but when the decree was modified in the First Appeal No 20 of 1981 by the judgment dated 07.07.1996 and the decree drawn on 03.11.1996, the decree holder opposite party ought to have taken steps in the execution case in aid of execution of the decree as modified, within three years from the said date or at least within the period of three years from the date of dismissal of the Civil petition for leave to Appeal no 689 of 1997 as such, although a review petition. being the Review petition no 14 of 1997 was filed which was dismissed for default on 06.11.2000 but the steps in aid of the execution case in Execution Case No 18 of 1980, being taken as late as on 08.08.2002, much beyond the period of limitation of 3 (three) years, the petition of the petitioners dated 15.09.2002 praying for dismissal of the execution case on the ground of limitation, was illegally rejected by the learned Joint District Judge by his order dated 28.09.2002 and is liable to be set aside. 

 4. On the other hand, Mr. Shafique Ahmed, Senior Advocate, appears with Mr. Md. Anwar Hossian, Advocate, on behalf of the decree holder opposite parties. He submits that they had no laches to file the execution case immediately after obtaining the decree in Title Suit on. 73 of 1976 being the Title Execution Case no. 18 of 1980 as early as on 26.11.1980 but the petitioner judgment debtors filed the First Appeal no 20 of 1981 and being unsuccessful took a further appeal before the Appellate Division being the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal no 689 of 1996 which was dismissed and thereafter filed a review petition being the Review Petition no 14 of 1997 which was also dismissed for default because of laches on his part on 06.11.2000 and thereafter within the period of limitation from that date necessary application was filed on 08.08.2002 to proceed with the execution case, as such, the learned Judge by his order dated 28.09.2002 rightly rejected the petition of the judgment-debtors to dismiss the Execution Case no 18 of 1980. The learned Advocate further submits referring to the decision in the case of Mymensingh Co-Operative Town Bank Ltd. Vs. Rajendra 12 DLR(1960)730, that an execution case will be within time if it is filed within 3 (three) years of the order passed in revision or review, as such, the application filed on 08.08.2002 in the Title Execution Case No. 18 of 1980 within the period of limitation of 3 (Three) years from the date of dismissed of the Review Application no 14 of 1997 for an default on 06.11.2000 and the learned Subordinate Judge rightly rejected the petition of the judgment debtors on 28.09.2002. 

 6. In the instant case, the suit was decreed on 30.091980 and the execution case was filed no 26.11.1980 (Annexure-A) but its proceedings was stayed on 19.12.1980, as directed by the High Court Division in Civil Rule No 1557(F) of 1980 in an appeal which was subsequently numbered as the First Appeal no 20 of 1981. The decree of the Trial Court was, however, modified by the High Court Division in its judgment and decree passed on 07.07.1996 (Decree drawn up on 03.11.1966), as such, in the normal course, the steps in aid, as envisaged in Art 182(5) of the limitation Act, for amendment of the petition of the execution case, ought to have been filed within 3(three) years from the date of the decree passed in appeal on 03.11.1996 but the operation of the said decree was also stayed by the Appellate Division in the Civil petition for leave to Appeal no 689 of 1996 which was however, dismissed on 16.03.1997 Although thereafter a review petition was filed before the Appellate division but no order of stay was given in the said review petition which was ultimately dismissed for default for non-compliance of the order of the Appellate division passed on 06.11.2000 after six weeks from the said date. 

 7. Since there was no order of stay either of the execution case or of the operation of the appellate decree, the period of limitation of 3 (three) years started to run from 16.03.1997 when the Civil petition for leave to Appeal No. 689 of 1996 was dismissed and the step in aid of the execution case as envisaged under Art. 182(5) of the limitation Act, became time-barred on the expiry of 15.03.2000. Since no step was taken to amend the petition of the execution case in commensurate with the decree as amended in appeal, within the period of limitation, the execution case itself is liable to be dismissed.
